overview: Jamaica is an island country in the Caribbean, south of Cuba. Its capital and largest city is Kingston. Jamaica became independent from the United Kingdom in 1962. It is the birthplace of reggae music and Bob Marley, and its sprinters, including Usain Bolt, have won many Olympic medals.

geography.text: Jamaica is the third-largest island in the Caribbean. Mountains run along the middle of the island, and the Blue Mountains in the east, where a famous coffee is grown, are the highest. Much of the island is limestone, with caves and underground rivers, and its coast is lined with beaches.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Tropical and warm, cooler in the Blue Mountains, with a hurricane season.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: The doctor bird, a hummingbird with a long tail, is the national bird.

history.text: Jamaica's Taíno people were wiped out after Spain arrived in 1494. Britain captured the island in 1655 and turned it into a major sugar colony worked by enslaved Africans, while people who escaped, known as Maroons, formed free communities in the mountains. Slavery ended in 1834, and Jamaica became independent in 1962.

events.title: Maroon treaty
events.text: The British sign a treaty recognising Maroon communities.

government.text: Jamaica is a constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth, with the British monarch as head of state, represented by a Governor-General. The Prime Minister leads the government. Jamaica has discussed becoming a republic.

economy.text: Tourism, money sent home from Jamaicans abroad and bauxite, the ore used to make aluminium, are major parts of the economy. Jamaica also exports coffee, including Blue Mountain coffee, and rum.

culture.text: Jamaica has had a huge influence on world music. Reggae, made famous by Bob Marley, is on UNESCO's heritage list, and ska, dub and dancehall also began there. Jamaican food such as jerk chicken and ackee and saltfish is popular worldwide.

items.title: Bob Marley
items.text: His album Exodus was named album of the century by Time magazine.

items.title: Jerk
items.text: Meat rubbed with spices and smoked over pimento wood.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Ackee and saltfish is the national dish; jerk chicken is famous worldwide.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Reggae, ska, dub and dancehall all began in Jamaica.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Emancipation Day and Independence Day in early August are celebrated with music and street parties.

sport.text: Jamaica is a sprinting superpower. Usain Bolt holds the world records in the 100 m and 200 m and won eight Olympic golds, and Shelly-Ann Fraser-Pryce and Elaine Thompson-Herah have dominated women's sprinting. Jamaica's bobsleigh team at the 1988 Winter Olympics inspired the film Cool Runnings.

items.title: Usain Bolt
items.text: 100 m world record of 9.58 seconds, set in 2009.
Jamaica's first bobsleigh team competed in Calgary.

items.title: Cricket
items.text: Jamaica plays as part of the West Indies.
